newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish govt seen likely to shuffle some officials.
newsitem.headline: Turkish govt seen likely to shuffle some officials.

text.p: Turkey's new right-left coalition government is expected to reshuffle senior economy officials after a confidence vote in parliament on July 12, government sources said on Wednesday.

The first sign of the move came on Wednesday when Haluk Gorgun replaced state-owned Vakifbank general manager Nazim Ekren, appointed by the former government of Necmettin Erbakan, the leader of the Islamist Welfare Party (RP).

Sources from Prime Minister Mesut Yilmaz's Motherland Party (ANAP) say former treasury deputy undersecretary Mahfi Egilmez, now working for a private company, has been offered the top treasury post, presently held by Mehmet Kaytaz.
Egilmez may then make his own changes in department personnel.
ANAP sources say central bank governor Gazi Ercel and Capital Markets Board chairman Ali Ihsan Karacan are expected to retain their duties.

However, Privatisation Administration chief Ismail Karakaya, who has headed agency since July 1996, may also lose his post in the reshuffle. Former privatisation head Ustun Sanver and deputy chairman Suleyman Yasar are considered to be among possible candidates for the post.
Prime Minister Yilmaz has asked state enterprises and local administrations to halt all new recruitments without permission from his office.
Housing Minister Yasar Topcu said he had moved to block the Islamist-led government plan to place its own supporters in key posts.
"We are correcting these appointments," Topcu told reporters. He said the former government gave its high ranking officials a free rein in appointments on its last day in power.
Yilmaz's three-party government is also likely to change senior managers of state banks.

"We are ready to hand over the post. (The government) has the right to establish the management structure it seeks to have here," Candan Karlitekin, general manager of Turkish Development Bank, told Reuters.
He was appointed as general manager in February.
